title: Master Cross-Corpus Concordance for Felix Klein (1872/1893 & 1895/1897)

entries.theme: Euclidean Straightedge-and-Compass Postulates & Iterated Square-Root Towers
entries.famous_problems_locus: Introduction & Part I, Ch. I (§§ 1–15, EN pp. 1–12 / DE S. 1–10)

sister_links.work: The Thirteen Books of Euclid's Elements (Heath, 1908)
sister_links.locus: Book I, Postulates 1–3; Book II, Prop. 14; Book VI, Props. 12–13
sister_links.relation: Klein's Fundamental Theorem (Hauptsatz) translates Euclid's Postulates 1–3 into the analytic closure of rational operations (+, -, *, /) and square roots sqrt(R).

sister_links.work: Methods and Theories for the Solution of Problems of Geometrical Constructions (1879)
sister_links.locus: Algebraic Appendix & Theorie der algebraischen Gleichungen (1878)
sister_links.relation: Klein explicitly singles out Julius Petersen in the Introduction (EN p. 2 / DE S. 2) as the sole textbook author presenting elementary algebraic impossibility proofs for geometric constructions.

sister_links.locus: Chapter VII (§§ 36–39: Geometrical Constructions Based Upon Axioms I–V)
sister_links.relation: Hilbert refines Klein's quadratic-tower criterion by isolating the Pythagorean subfield (sqrt(1 + omega^2), solvable with straightedge and segment-transferrer Eichmass) inside the full Euclidean square-root field.

entries.theme: Delian Cube Duplication, Angle Trisection, and Plane vs. Solid Problems

sister_links.locus: Book III (Delian Mean Proportionals) & Book IV (Plane, Solid, and Linear Problems; Conchoid Trisection)
sister_links.relation: Klein's degree-2^h impossibility proofs for x^3 = 2 and x^3 = cos(phi) + i*sin(phi), paired with conic intersections, Diocles' cissoid, and Nicomedes' conchoid in Ch. V, supply the exact Galois-algebraic proof of Pappus's ancient classification of plane, solid, and linear loci.

sister_links.work: The Thirteen Books of Euclid's Elements (Heath, 1908)
sister_links.locus: Book I, Prop. 9 (Angle Bisection) & Book XI, Props. 31–33 (Parallelepipeds & Cubes)
sister_links.relation: Contrasts elementary quadratic angle bisection (Euclid I.9) with the irreducible cubic monodromy of general angle trisection.

entries.theme: Cyclotomy, Kepler's Unknowable Heptagon (n = 7), and Gauss's Heptadecagon (n = 17)

sister_links.locus: Book I, Props. XLV–XLVII (De heptagono et figuris inscibilibus)
sister_links.relation: Kepler argued philosophically and algebraically that the regular heptagon (n = 7) is 'unknowable' (inscibilis) because its side ratio obeys a cubic equation irreducible to planar bisections; Klein Ch. III (§§ 5–7) proves rigorouly via Eisenstein's criterion that z^6 + ... + 1 = 0 (real cubic u^3 + u^2 - 2u - 1 = 0) has degree 6 != 2^h, while p = 17 = 2^(2^2) + 1 splits into four quadratics.

sister_links.work: The Thirteen Books of Euclid's Elements (Heath, 1908)
sister_links.relation: Klein Ch. III, § 2 explains Euclid IV.16 (regular 15-gon) arithmetically via Bezout partial fractions 1/15 = 2/3 - 3/5.

entries.theme: Restricted Instruments: Poncelet–Steiner Fixed Circle, Mascheroni Compasses, and Geometrography
entries.famous_problems_locus: Part I, Ch. IV (§§ 7–9, EN pp. 33–41 / DE S. 25–32) & Ch. V (§ 1, Paper Folding)

sister_links.work: Géométrographie, ou Art des constructions géométriques (1902)
sister_links.locus: Part I (Operational Symbols R_1, R_2, C_1, C_2, C_3) & Poncelet-Steiner / Mascheroni Comparisons
sister_links.relation: Klein's sharp distinction between theoretical instrument classes—straightedge alone (rational field), Mascheroni compasses alone, and Poncelet–Steiner–von Staudt–Schröter straightedge + one fixed circle—parallels Lemoine's quantitative operational measure of ruler vs. compass simplicity.
Pure straightedge constructions (Lambert, Brianchon, von Staudt) construct precisely projective rational functions via harmonic ranges, requiring one fixed metric circle C_0 to adjoin square roots.

entries.theme: Cantor's Continuum, Transcendence of e and pi, and Quadrature of the Circle
entries.famous_problems_locus: Part II, Chs. I–V (EN pp. 49–80 / DE S. 38–66)

sister_links.work: The Principles of Mathematics (1903) & An Essay on the Foundations of Geometry (1897)
sister_links.locus: PoM Part V (Infinity and Continuity, Cantor's Aleph_0 vs. Continuum) & Part VI
sister_links.relation: Klein's exposition of Cantor's countability of algebraic numbers by height N and diagonal uncountability of the continuum (Part II, Ch. I) anticipates Russell's Cantorian resolution of spatial continuity in 1903.

sister_links.locus: Caput III (§ 2.6, Continuous Extension vs. Point-Sets) & Caput VII
sister_links.relation: Contrasts point-set enumerations of algebraic vs. transcendental coordinates with intuitive continuous geometric extension traced by mechanical curve-integrators (Integraph, Ch. V).

entries.theme: The Erlangen Hierarchy: Principal Group, Affine Geometry, and Projective Collineations
entries.famous_problems_locus: Part I, Ch. IV (§ 7, Rational Projective vs. Quadratic Euclidean Operations)

sister_links.relation: Elevates Pappus's cross-ratio invariance from an isolated synthetic lemma to the defining invariant of the projective collineation group encompassing the Principal Group.

sister_links.locus: Chapters V–VI (Desargues's & Pascal's Theorems) & 1902 Appendix on Transformation Groups
sister_links.relation: Connects Klein's continuous group hierarchy directly to Hilbert's axiomatic Characterization of Desarguesian skew-fields, Pappian commutative fields, and Helmholtz–Lie transformation axioms.

entries.theme: Cayley–Klein Projective Metrics, the Absolute Quadric, and Rational Trigonometry
entries.erlangen_locus: §§ 1–2, § 6, § 10.2 & Note V (On the So-Called Non-Euclidean Geometry)

sister_links.locus: Quadrance, Spread, Cross-Ratio, and Projective Null Conic Metrics
sister_links.relation: Wildberger's quadrance Q and spread s strip away transcendental logarithms from Klein's Cayley–Klein metric d(A,B) = c*log(A,B;I_1,I_2), expressing Principal, hyperbolic, elliptic, and Möbius invariants as pure rational functions over Q.

sister_links.work: An Essay on the Foundations of Geometry (1897) & Principles of Mathematics (1903)
sister_links.locus: EFG Ch. I (§§ 30–43: Cayley & Klein) & PoM Ch. XLVIII (§§ 405–411: Projective Theory of Distance)
sister_links.relation: Russell explicitly adopts Klein's 1871–1872 projective classification of hyperbolic, elliptic, and parabolic geometries relative to the Absolute while debating whether cross-ratio metrics replace philosophical intuition of distance.

sister_links.locus: Caput II–IV (Critique of Non-Euclidean Projective Interpretations & Structuralism)
sister_links.relation: Hoenen examines Klein's Principle of Transference (§§ 4–5) and Cayley–Klein models (Note V), arguing that relative consistency inside projective Euclidean models presupposes an intuitive ambient continuum.

entries.theme: Reciprocal Radii (Möbius Inversion), Plücker Line Geometry, and Lie's Sphere Geometry
entries.famous_problems_locus: Part I, Ch. V (§§ 3–4: CircularPoints at Infinity on Cissoid & Conchoid)

sister_links.work: Methods and Theories for the Solution of Problems of Geometrical Constructions (1879)
sister_links.locus: Chapter III (Method of Rotation, Similarity, and Inversion / Reciprocal Radii)
sister_links.relation: Petersen's constructive problem-solving transformations (translation, rotation, homothety, circle inversion) instantiate in planar synthesis the exact subgroups systematized in §§ 1 & 6 of Klein's Erlangen Program.

sister_links.locus: Transformation by Reciprocal Radii & Apollonius Contact Constructions
sister_links.relation: Links Lie's contact geometry of tangency among circles and spheres (§ 7) to classical Apollonius contact constructions.
